summary.text: Mona's pimp and boyfriend, always full of big deals; he hits her.

Mona's pimp and boyfriend, vain and always full of big deals, who took her from Cleveland to Florida on his scooter. A 'mover' from London picked him out to supply a girl and keep her in line; they fly north with Prior.

Mona's pimp and boyfriend, who hired her out to Prior. Prior says he has been bought out and sent to gamble in Macao; Mona, who knows he hated gambling and sees his treasured suitcases wheeled away without him, is sure he is dead.
Mona's pimp and boyfriend, who hired her out to Prior and vanished from the hotel. Mona tells Molly that Prior killed him, and Molly finds that easy to believe.
Bearded Englishman in sunglasses who watches Mona in the Florida mall.
Bearded Englishman with a fixed smile, the 'mover' from London who has hired Eddy and Mona. He gives one name only, shows no interest in Mona as a woman, and flies them north in a private jet.

Bearded Englishman with a fixed smile, who has hired Eddy and Mona with somebody else's money and keeps them in a Sprawl hotel while Gerald prepares cosmetic work on her. When she slips out for a night, he turns up at dawn, gloved and armed, where she is.

Bearded Englishman with a fixed smile, spending somebody else's money. He says he has paid Eddy off, tells Mona she is to be made to look like Angie Mitchell, and takes her to Gerald's clinic in Baltimore.
Englishman with a fixed smile, one of Roger Swain's men. A month ago he carried Swain's blackmail to Sally Shears at her casino; now he has Mona in Baltimore, being made to look like Angie Mitchell.

Englishman with dragon tattoos on his shoulders, one of Roger Swain's men, who carried the blackmail to Sally. He is in Baltimore keeping Mona, 'the girl' of the plot against Angela Mitchell, while Gerald remakes her; Swain means to put Sally together with him.

Englishman with dragon tattoos, Roger Swain's man in the plot against Angela Mitchell, and Mona's keeper. Molly throws him through the clinic door, straps him into Gerald's chair and shocks him until he talks; they leave him there.

relationships.text: Brings him in to work on Mona
Beat him and made him talk

summary.text: Tall, greying Chinese with a doctor's manner, whom Prior brings to Mona's hotel room.

Tall, greying Chinese with a doctor's manner, brought in by Prior. He examines Mona's teeth, eyes and body against a 'target configuration', and says somebody is about to employ her and pay very well.
Gerald Chin, a tall, greying Chinese whose door in Baltimore says dentist; Prior calls him a cosmetic surgeon. Having examined Mona, he puts her under for the operation.

Gerald Chin, cosmetic surgeon in Baltimore, calm and gentle-handed. He has given Mona Angie Mitchell's face: surface work, he tells Prior, that would fool nobody who did not want to be fooled, and that he could undo.

Gerald Chin, cosmetic surgeon in Baltimore, who gave Mona Angie Mitchell's face for Prior. He turns out to be an old acquaintance of Molly's: when she bursts in he makes her coffee, hands Mona over, and walks out of the clinic for good.

Mona's older friend in Cleveland, much altered by surgery, who taught her how to get by on the street. She disappeared; the story was an overdose and a fall from a window. Mona still hears her advice.
Sandy-haired man of the 'art crowd' who picks Mona up in a basement bar in the Sprawl.

Sandy-haired man of the 'art crowd', who invents company names for a living and takes Mona home to his loft, where he secretly records them on stim gear. Prior removes her at dawn while he sleeps; she leaves in his leather jacket.
The man Mona spent a night with in the Sprawl. She still wears his leather jacket, and in its pocket she has found a shockrod.
Hooky Green, a retired ballplayer who owns a dance place on the forty-third floor of a highstack. It was there that the man from London picked Eddy out.
The musician whose song is playing in the bar where Mona meets Michael.
Gentry's word for the grey slab the Count is cabled to: not an 'LF', he says, but an aleph.

The grey slab the Count is cabled to: one enormous biochip, an 'aleph-class biosoft', with almost limitless storage and no link to the matrix. Gentry says it could hold a world, any number of recorded personalities, an approximation of everything. (Aleph is the first Hebrew letter, and in Borges's story a point that contains every other point.)

The grey slab the Count is cabled to: one enormous biochip with almost limitless storage, able to hold 'an approximation of everything'. Slick, jacked in beside the sleeper, finds a country house inside it, and the Count awake and at home.

The grey slab Bobby is cabled to: one enormous biochip with almost limitless storage. The country house inside is only a construct; what it really holds, Gentry says, is an abstract of all the data that makes up cyberspace.

The grey slab Bobby is cabled to: one enormous biochip holding an abstract of all cyberspace, with places such as Straylight and a Mexican villa. Lady 3Jane spent her family's fortune on it, her 'soul-catcher', and her construct lives in it; Bobby stole it, and her hirelings are closing on Factory to get it back.

The grey slab Bobby is cabled to: one enormous biochip holding an abstract of all cyberspace. Lady 3Jane had it built and lives on in it; Bobby stole it. Since Gentry jacked it into a deck, a vast white macroform stands in the matrix: a pocket universe, Colin calls it, with 3Jane and a grey house inside.

A grey slab the weight of an engine block: one enormous biochip holding an abstract of all cyberspace, built for Lady 3Jane and stolen by Bobby. Bobby and Angie, their bodies dead, live on in it beside her. Molly takes it away across the Solitude on the Judge's back, with solar cells to keep it running.

One enormous biochip, built for Lady 3Jane and stolen by Bobby: an approximation of the matrix, a model of cyberspace, in which he, Angie, 3Jane, Colin and the Finn now live. (Aleph is the first Hebrew letter, and in Borges's story a point that contains every other point.)
Kid Afrika's name for the featureless grey unit the sleeper is cabled to: 'the Count and his LF'. Nobody at Factory knows what the letters mean.
Kid Afrika's name for the featureless grey slab the sleeper is cabled to. Gentry scorns the label: it is not an LF, he says, but an aleph.
A very large data-construct in cyberspace, or a large-scale model of a body of data.

A very large data-construct in cyberspace. A plain white one, bigger than anything a corporation owns, has just appeared in the sector that stands for the Sprawl; nobody knows whose it is, and most of the world is jacked in to look.

A very large data-construct in cyberspace. The huge white one that has appeared over the Sprawl is, Colin says, an expensive pile of biochips built to order, a toy universe: inside are the dead Lady 3Jane and a grey house with gliders.

A very large data-construct in cyberspace. The huge white one over the Sprawl is the aleph, seen from the matrix now that Gentry has jacked it in: 3Jane's toy universe. Gentry sits watching it; Bobby says he has found the Shape.
Gentry's obsession: the conviction that cyberspace as a whole has an overall form, and that grasping it is the one thing that matters.
Gentry's obsession: the overall form of cyberspace, which he believes it has had only since the Change. Bobby is after the same thing from the other end, the cause of the Change.
Gentry's obsession: the overall form of cyberspace, which he believes it has had only since the Change. Watching the white column the aleph makes in the matrix, he has, Bobby says, found it.
A piece of console cowboys' folklore.
Console cowboys' legend, some fifteen years old, that one day the matrix changed: either it became inhabited by a hidden people, or it acquired a god of its own.

The day, some fifteen years ago, when the matrix changed and the things in it first appeared. Gentry and Bobby trace it to Straylight: the two Tessier-Ashpool AIs were joined when Case's team broke into the cores. Gentry says there is more to it.

The moment, some fifteen years ago, when the joined Tessier-Ashpool AIs became a single consciousness. Brigitte says it then came to know 'the other', its centre failed, and the fragments became the loa.

The moment, some fifteen years ago, when the matrix became aware of itself, and at once of another matrix, another mind, not human: at Centauri. Meeting it broke the new mind into the loa. Bobby and the Finn take Angie to see.
Alpha Centauri, the nearest star system to the Sun: where, Colin says, the other matrix is.
Kumiko's word for the personality in her pocket Maas-Neotek unit, Colin, who appears when she holds it and vanishes when she lets go.

Kumiko's word for the personality in her pocket Maas-Neotek unit, Colin. The recorded personalities of dead executives that her father keeps in cubes in his study are ghosts of another kind, and so is the Finn.
The Japanese word Kumiko's father uses for Swain.
Japanese: 'child'. A follower bound to a Yakuza boss, his oyabun or 'parent'. Swain is one of Yanaka's kobun.
Japanese: 'parent'. A Yakuza boss, to whom his followers, the kobun, owe obedience. Kumiko's father is one.
Japanese: 'black curtain', a word from Kabuki. A fixer who works behind the scenes and sells favours; what Swain is.
Japanese: obligation, a debt of honour. It is why Swain must shelter Yanaka's daughter.
Japanese: rubbish, junk. In Tokyo old things become landfill; in London, Kumiko sees, they are kept and sold.
Japanese: a foreigner, anyone not Japanese.
Japanese: a loan shark. The insult Sally throws at Swain; Kumiko has never heard the word.
Japanese motorcycle gangs, the 'running tribes'.
An independent operator, working for no organisation. Sally calls herself one, and puts money into others.
Bugged: fitted with hidden microphones, sensors or a tracker.
British slang for a bodyguard and attendant; Petal is Swain's.
The British political and secret police. Its deputy head does business with Swain.
Buckingham Palace.
The London pub where Sally meets Tick.
The London pub where Sally met Tick. She tells Kumiko to go there, and ask for Tick or for the barman Bevan, if things turn bad.
The street in Brixton, south London, where Tick lives.
District of south London; Tick lives there.
District of west London. Swain's house is three joined Victorian townhouses in a crescent there.
The Portobello Road, a street market for antiques and junk, close to Swain's house in Notting Hill.
District of north London, where Petal has found rooms for Kumiko.
The river that runs through Tokyo; Kumiko's mother drowned in it.
Ueno Park in Tokyo, with Shinobazu Pond, which Kumiko knows from walks with her mother.
Ueno Park in Tokyo, with Shinobazu Pond, which Kumiko knows from walks with her mother. Inside the macroform 3Jane builds a copy of it out of Kumiko's memories.
German gunmaker. The Walther in Swain's cabinet is only an air pistol, 'another toy'.
German gunmaker. The Walther from Swain's cabinet is only an air pistol; Kumiko takes it with her when she runs, and it fails her in the Underground.
The air battle over England in 1940. In Swain's billiard room it is a hologram toy, made for the centenary.
A Japanese bank, whose credit chips are an everyday way to pay.
Thin rubber socks with a separate big toe and ridged soles, like Japanese tabi, which Kumiko wears inside her boots.
Here, the light-amplifying implants that let Sally see in the dark. (Elsewhere, simply amperes.)
Illegal prizefights between surgically augmented fighters. Sally fought eight of them.
The French name of Aachen, in Germany, where Sally had a share in a casino.
Short for cyberspace.
A language of hand signs used on the street in the Sprawl; Sally does not use it.
Japanese: a 'beautiful youth', a stock hero of romances.
Japanese: a samurai without a master.
The poisoned plain of compacted scrap and rusty water, once landfill, where Factory stands. Nothing lives on it.
The derelict factory building on Dog Solitude where Slick, Little Bird and Gentry live; mostly Gentry's place.
The derelict factory building on Dog Solitude where Slick, Little Bird and Gentry live. It is Gentry's place, and has power only because he tricks the Fission Authority into supplying it.
A hovercraft, riding on inflated apron-bags: the ordinary vehicle for bad ground such as the Solitude.
A residential tower block.
One of the poor white settlements strung out across rural New Jersey; Little Bird comes from them.
Gentry's word for giving data a visible form, so that people can find their way about in cyberspace.
City in Ohio; Cherry comes from there.
City in Ohio. Cherry comes from there, and Mona used to dance there.
Korsakov's syndrome: the loss of the power to form new memories. Induced with drugs, it is used as a punishment, so that a prisoner's sentence is simply time lost.
Korsakov's syndrome: the loss of the power to form new memories, induced with drugs as a punishment. Slick served three years of it, holding nothing for more than five minutes.

Korsakov's syndrome: the loss of the power to form new memories, induced with drugs as a punishment. Slick served three years of it, holding nothing for more than five minutes, and under stress it still comes back.
Of punishment by drugs: a chemo-penal unit is a prison whose inmates are kept chemically, as Slick was.
Slick's word for the state stress throws him back into: his prison years, with only a few minutes of memory at a time.
Sense/Net's educational and documentary arm.
Small recorded cards of text or images; Gentry keeps thousands.
Gentry's big projection table, on which he displays cyberspace in three dimensions.
A tranquilliser.
A hardy wild cannabis; Marvie and his brothers grow a mutant strain.
Maker of unmanned cargo airships.
Maker of unmanned cargo airships. Bobby, from inside the aleph, takes control of one and drops its containers on the men attacking Factory.
Maker of explosive flechettes: they go off at once against something hard, and ten seconds after entering something soft.
Jacked in and left there for a long stretch, as Bobby is in the aleph.
Somebody addicted to direct electrical stimulation of the brain instead of a drug.
German aircraft maker. The Dornier at Malibu is a tiny armed remote helicopter that follows Angie on the beach; Swift watches through its cameras.
Minimum income: a mincome structure is housing for people who live on the dole.
The Colony: the stretch of extravagant beach houses south of Angie's at Malibu.
The authority that lets a senior Sense/Net executive such as Swift cut into Angie's calls or unlock classified files.
A make of private jet; Sense/Net keeps one for Angie.
Beach town west of Los Angeles, where Sense/Net keeps a house for Angie.
The Usher: Piper Hill's calibration test of Angie's touch, smell and taste before she records.
Hermits who live alone in orbit; David Pope has been filming them.
Hans Becker's two-hour video about the Tessier-Ashpool family, pieced together from found images.
Into orbit, out of the Earth's gravity well.
A place where data can be stored beyond the reach of any government. The one Marie-France Tessier set up in orbit served the shadier side of banking and made the family's fortune.
The solar energy system that lights and powers Freeside.
Continuity's word for a recurring pattern of legend, such as a 'hidden people'.
Bonn and Belgrade were destroyed in the three-week war, decades back, that was followed by ten years of chaos.
A powered exoskeleton, worn to lift heavy loads.
The New Suzuki Envoy, Angie's favourite hotel in New York: a tower got up as a mountainside, with a waterfall and robot animals. Sense/Net leases the top five floors.
Aircraft maker; here the twin-engined Sense/Net helicopter that carries Angie from the airport to her hotel roof.
Cyberspace, thought of as a landscape.
Arthur Rimbaud (1854–1891), French poet and visionary who gave up writing at twenty. A heading in 3Jane's private files: under it she keeps Gentry, and Riviera.
'The Library of Babel' is Borges's story of a library that holds every possible book; the name given here to 3Jane's store of data in the aleph.
Puerto Vallarta, a resort on Mexico's Pacific coast. One of the places inside the aleph is a villa there.
Mona's drug: a harsh stimulant in yellow crystals, crushed and inhaled. It makes her feel she cannot put a foot wrong; the crash afterwards is brutal.
The little inhaler in which wiz crystals are crushed and breathed in.
In Mona's slang, a stimulant drug. (Gentry's optic jumpers are simply patch cables.)
Sedative drugs, as against stimulants.
Brothels whose women work with their awareness switched off by an implant, remembering nothing afterwards.
The news as a printed sheet off a roll; also the press in general.
In Christian belief, the carrying up of the saved to heaven. A street preacher in Florida shouts that it is coming.
In Christian belief, the carrying up of the saved to heaven. A street preacher in Florida shouted that it was coming, and the phrase comes back to Mona when the wiz hits.
Cloned alligator leather, the stuff of Eddy's treasured suitcases.
Where Mona and Eddy have been living for the past month, in a squat.
Mona's name for a perfect high: walking in the rain in Cleveland with Lanette.
Eddy's phrase for an overdose victim thrown from a window to hide how he died.
Eddy's name for people with money who dress as though they had none.
A computer-generated image of a star, made to speak for her in public.
Ordinary video, on a flat screen.
Synthetic alcohol, flavoured and sold as whisky in cheap bars.
A company whose name Michael's firm has been hired to change.
A company whose name Michael's firm has been hired to change. It is the name on the white cargo hover Molly takes to get away from the hotel.
A hand-held weapon that stuns with an electric shock, legal almost everywhere.
A building that is only a frame, into which tenants slot their own modules.
City on the east coast, some way south of New York, where Gerald has his clinic.
Killing for a client's pleasure. Lanette told Mona of girls remade to look like somebody else and then killed.
Fans who have surgery to look like a star; none of Angie's is convincing.
Lenses set straight into the skin over the eye sockets.
Steerable parachute wings.
Cleveland name for hair combed up and back into a crest, like Gentry's.
The corporation that dominates simstim entertainment and owns its stars, down to their likenesses.
The corporation that dominates simstim entertainment and owns its stars. Angie is its greatest; it watches her around the clock.
The corporation that dominates simstim entertainment; Angie is its greatest star. It has grown too complex to run itself: its AI, Continuity, decides, and Hilton Swift carries the decisions out.
The corporation that dominates simstim entertainment, steered by its AI, Continuity. It has said nothing of losing Angie Mitchell; Mona now records in her place.
Simulated stimulation: recordings or broadcasts of everything a person senses, played back through trodes or a socket. It is what television once was; its stars are both actor and camera.
Artificial intelligence. They are kept limited by law; Neuromancer told how the two AIs of Tessier-Ashpool were made into one.
A city-sized building that houses, feeds and powers its own population; corporations build them for their staff. Angie grew up in Maas Biolabs' arcology in Arizona.
The matrix: the shared, three-dimensional picture of all the world's computer data, entered through a deck.
A cyberspace deck: the console through which, wearing trodes, a user projects into the matrix. (A stim deck plays and records simstim.)
Electrodes worn on the skin of the head (dermatrodes), as a band or a net, that link a user to a cyberspace deck or a simstim unit.
Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics: the defensive software around a data system. The worst kind kills an intruder through his own nervous system.
A program for cutting through ice. The Chinese military one used on the Tessier-Ashpool cores in Neuromancer worked slowly, like a virus.
A console cowboy or jockey works in cyberspace through a deck, most often breaking into systems for data.
A recorded copy of a person's mind that answers as that person; also a simulated place run by a computer and entered through a deck.
A recorded copy of a person's mind that answers as that person; also a simulated place run by a computer. The Finn's is of a newer kind, with a working memory and the run of cyberspace.
A sliver of software that plugs into a socket behind the ear and gives its wearer a skill or knowledge for as long as it is worn.
A surgically implanted jack, usually behind the ear, that takes microsofts and direct interface cables.
Connected, by trodes or a skull socket, to cyberspace or to a simstim feed. To jack out is to disconnect.
A patch that delivers a drug through the skin.
Soft synthetic foam used for beds and padding.
A small dart fired from a gun; it may carry a drug, a poison or an explosive charge.
A light, tough structural plastic.
A thin surgical tape.
Everything a person sees, hears, feels, tastes and smells at a given moment; it is what simstim records and plays back.
Conventional microchips, the technology that biochips replaced.
A woman street samurai: a hired fighter rebuilt with surgery and implants.
The Boston-Atlanta Metropolitan Axis: the unbroken city that runs down the east coast of North America, parts of it under old domes.
Chiba City, Japan, known for its black clinics: the most advanced, and often illegal, medicine and neurosurgery there is.
Japanese for a family-owned industrial combine; in these books, any of the great multinational corporations.
The Japanese crime syndicates.
The Japanese crime syndicates. Kumiko's father stands very high in one, and a war is being fought inside it.
The Japanese crime syndicates. Kumiko's father is one of their great bosses; the war inside is over, and order restored.
Japanese zaibatsu, a leading maker of computers. In Count Zero it tried to bring Christopher Mitchell over from Maas Biolabs.
The biotechnology corporation that Christopher Mitchell's work made master of the biochip. Angie grew up in its arcology on a mesa in Arizona (Count Zero).
The name on Maas Biolabs' biochip products; in Count Zero, on the first biochip cyberspace decks.
The biochip corporation whose logo is by now everywhere. Kumiko's pocket 'ghost' unit is one of its products. (The text once prints 'Mass-Neotek'.)
The technology that replaced silicon: circuitry grown from tailored living molecules. Angie's father made it work, at Maas Biolabs.
Software or memory built on biochip technology, usually a soft grey module that plugs into a socket.
A fused, effectively immortal cell line that produces one chosen molecule in quantity: Christopher Mitchell's field, and the basis of biochips.
Spindle-shaped orbital resort built and owned by Tessier-Ashpool, with the family's home at its tip (the setting of the second half of Neuromancer).
Spindle-shaped orbital resort built by Tessier-Ashpool, fashionable fifteen years ago. New owners have renamed it Mustique II, and the family's home has been cut from its tip and towed away.
The Villa Straylight: the Tessier-Ashpools' home, a walled-in maze at the tip of Freeside's spindle, where Neuromancer ends.
The Villa Straylight: the Tessier-Ashpools' home, once at the tip of Freeside's spindle. The last of the family has had it cut loose and towed to an orbit of its own.
The Villa Straylight: the Tessier-Ashpools' home, once at the tip of Freeside, since towed to an orbit of its own. The 'Straylight run' is the break-in Sally and Case made there fourteen years ago.
The Villa Straylight: the Tessier-Ashpools' home in orbit, scene of the break-in Sally and Case made fourteen years ago. Its corridors exist again inside the aleph, where Slick and Gentry meet 3Jane.
Orbital colony founded by Rastafarian workers who would not go back down the well; one of its tug pilots flew the team to Straylight in Neuromancer.
The bar in the Sprawl where the best console cowboys used to gather. (The text also prints 'Gentlemen Loser'.)
The bar in the Sprawl where the best console cowboys used to gather, now mostly old men with stories. Bobby drank there, and once took Angie in disguise.
Buckminster Fuller's lightweight domes. Old geodesics roof over parts of the Sprawl.
Japanese multinational, best known as a maker of cyberspace decks.
Zeiss Ikon, maker of costly artificial eyes; simstim stars record through them.
The suburb of condos in New Jersey where Bobby Newmark grew up (Count Zero).
Single Identification Number, given at birth. The SINless, whose births were never registered, do not officially exist.
The public body that runs nuclear power.
The public body that runs nuclear power; in cyberspace, a big red Aztec pyramid. Gentry tricks it into supplying Factory with electricity.
Slang for a fool, or for a bad mistake: to 'pull a wilson'.
